Convert latent GP predictions to the requested prediction type

Source: R/gpPredictFromLatent.R
gpPredictFromLatent.Rd

gpPredictFromLatent() is an internal helper used by prediction functions that have already computed latent predictions for f. It applies the common type = "latent", "terms", and "response" prediction logic used by predict.gp().

gpPredictFromLatent(
  gp,
  pred,
  data,
  type = c("latent", "terms", "response"),
  hyperpar = gpHyperparList(gp),
  se.fit = FALSE,
  cov.fit = FALSE,
  pred.cov = NULL,
  conf.int = FALSE,
  conf.level = 0.95
)

Arguments

gp

Object of class gp.

pred

Matrix or data frame with column f, and optionally f_SE. The rows must initially be in the dimension of gp$GP_factor.

data

Object of class gpData to pass to the likelihood template. The caller must provide data on the scale expected by the template.

type

Character; prediction type. Same meaning as in predict.gp().

hyperpar

List of hyperparameter values, usually from gpHyperparList(gp). When likelihood hyperparameters are present in the model (fixed or fitted), it must already contain the .lik component with correct hyperparameter values.

se.fit

Logical; should standard errors be present in the returned prediction matrix? If TRUE and pred has no f_SE column, pred.cov must be supplied.

cov.fit

Logical; should the latent covariance matrix be returned?

pred.cov

Optional covariance matrix of latent predictions, in the same row order as pred before any likelihood-template reindexing.

conf.int

Logical; should latent-scale confidence interval columns be added? Same meaning as in predict.gp().

conf.level

Numeric confidence level used when conf.int = TRUE.

Value

If cov.fit = FALSE, a prediction matrix. If cov.fit = TRUE, a list with components pred and cov, matching predict.gp().

For type = "latent", predictions remain in the dimension of gp$GP_factor. For type = "terms" or type = "response", predictions are reindexed to the main table when gp$lik.reindex2main requires it. In that reindexed case, cov.fit = TRUE is currently not supported, matching predict.gp().
